answer: Use clear [-f] topology [target=]<value>. It manually removes existing topology neighbor information. The target may be an lldp-neighbor instance (discovered via LLDP), a carrier-neighbor instance (discovered via ICMP), or an lldp-port-statistics instance (details associated with an LLDP enabled port). target is an instance-identifier and is used only with clear; there is no default. The -f flag forces the command without confirmation. Tip: type 'clear topology <tab>' to list valid topology objects. Example: clear topology lldp-neighbor-ethernet-1-4-T1-1. The companion show topology takes inci, links, lldp, icdp or sndp. Access mode is Operational Mode; Candidate Configuration Mode only for the show command.

Use verify [-f] [type-select=]<value> [[target-select=]<value>] [allow-switching]. type-select currently supports only fiber-connection. target-select is the port instance-identifier of the CableID-capable card; if omitted, verification runs on all paths. If the port is in multiple CableID paths, all of them are checked. allow-switching is boolean, default false: false verifies active paths only (no system initiated switching), true lets CableID initiate switching on the OPSM so active and inactive paths are both verified, so use false when the system is in service. Pre-condition: equipment-policies cable-id-control must be enabled. The command prompts for confirmation (-f skips it), raises the CID-verification-in-progress alarm against the NE, and is non-blocking: check progress with show cable-id-status. Example: verify fiber-connection port-1-6-ade3 allow-switching=true.

Use the bert command in Operational Mode: bert start test-id=TestX resource=ethernet-1-6-T1 test-signal-type=scrambled-idles test-signal-monitoring-type=scrambled-idles test-signal-direction=ingress test-signal-monitoring-direction=egress test-duration=10, then bert stop test-id=TestX. test-id is alphanumeric and is system generated if you omit it, but it is mandatory for bert stop. test-signal-type: none (default), PRBS31, PRBS31NONINV, scrambled-idles; 100GE/400GE use scrambled-idles, ODU4 uses PRBS31/PRBS31NONINV. test-signal-monitoring-type adds fec-frames (CarrierCTP). Directions are ingress or egress. test-duration is in seconds, min 10 up to 1000 hrs; default 0 means indefinite. Also bert get and bert delete by test-id, resource or AID. Multiple simultaneous BERTs may run on a facility if each meets the pre-conditions.

The cid-ptp facility is created by the system when a card supporting the CableID function is created, for example RD20TM or CAD10A; managed-by is system and only user-created facilities can be user deleted, so you do not create it yourself. It supports the CableID SFP and its connection to the card via the CID port. Only set and show are offered: set cid-ptp-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] and show cid-ptp-<name> with supporting-card, supporting-port, AID, oper-state, avail-state, managed-by, used. admin-state is not editable, the only supported value is unlock, and CableID operation is not affected by it. used is true when CableID functionality is supported (default false). label is a string 0..256. Example: show cid-ptp-1-4-spcid or show cid-ptp-1-6-spu. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode.

The Digital Coherent 400ZR eth-zr facility is auto-instantiated when the ZR TOM is provisioned; interface-type shows 400ZR (Media-interface 400ZR-CFEC-DP-16QAM) and rate is 400.000 Gbit/s. fec-type is settable with values not-applicable, cfec, ofec, noFEC, G709, i4, i7, sdfec15, sdfec15nd, staircase7, ufec7; default is ofec. Degrade thresholds are in average BER over range 0.000000001..0.1: fdd-threshold default 0.0195, fdd-clear-threshold default 0.01062, fed-threshold default 0.0206, fed-clear-threshold default 0.01125. fdd-monitoring and fed-monitoring are enabled/disabled, default disabled. link-degrade-indication shows none, local-degraded, remote-degraded or local-and-remote-degraded. Example: set eth-zr-1-6-T8 fed-threshold 0.011870000.

The ethernet facility attribute max-packet-length sets the maximum transfer unit in octets. On the 1830 GX G30 the range is 1280..18000 octets; on the 1830 GX G40 the range is 1518..18000 octets. The default is 1518. Set it with set ethernet-<name> max-packet-length <value> and read it with show ethernet-<name> max-packet-length. Two restrictions apply: max-packet-length is configurable on card level only and applies to all interfaces in that card, and it is used only for determining the undersized/oversized packet count in 100GbE PMs. Access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Use show facilities. It displays the system facilities, that is the list of facilities currently present on the node. It takes no parameters, and the only form is show facilities; access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. On a 1830 GX G40 node the output lists instances such as super-channel-group-1-4-L1, super-channel-1-4-L1-1, optical-carrier-1-4-L1-1, optical-channel-1-4-L1-1, trib-ptp-1-4-T11, comm-channel-1-4-L1-1, otu-1-4-L1-1-OTUCni, otu-1-4-T11, ethernet-1-4-T2, odu-1-4-L1-1-ODUCni and odu-1-4-L2-1-ODUflexi-1. For per-facility detail, run the show command of the individual facility type, for example show ethernet-1-4-T2.

The fc facility (set fc-<name> / show fc-<name>) carries the Fibre Channel specific settings. fc-type is read-only and reports FC1G, FC2G, FC4G, FC8G, FC16G or FC32G. tts enables or disables Transmitter Training Signal support for the 32GFC client, values enabled/disabled, default disabled. laser-toggling-for-tts enables or disables laser toggling when tts is enabled or disabled for the 32GFC client, values enabled/disabled, default enabled. The rest are the common facility attributes: label, admin-state (lock/unlock/maintenance, default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed), tx-mapping-mode and expected-mapping-mode (GMP default, BMP, openZR+, FlexE-4x100G, GFP-F, GFP-F-extOPU2, AMP, iGMP, none), loopback (none/facility/terminal), loopback-mode, test-signal-type, test-signal-direction (default ingress) and test-signal-monitoring.

On the flexo facility, foic-type is a read-only attribute showing the FOICx.k interface: foic1.2, foic1.4, foic2.4, foic2.8, foic3.6, foic4.8 and foic4.16, default foic4.8. FOICx.k means k parallel lanes carrying a FlexO-x interface, where order x is the rate in units of 100G, per G.709.3 FlexO-LR and G.709.1 FlexO-SR. fec-type is also read-only with values not-applicable, cfec, ofec and noFEC, default ofec. resource-mode is settable and selects the resource mode: ADM for add-drop, XC for add-drop with regen; default is ADM. Example: set flexo-1-5-L1-1 resource-mode 'XC'. Other settable attributes are label, admin-state, alarm-report-control, iid and the fdd/fed raise and clear thresholds. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode.

add flexo-group-<name> requires four mandatory attributes: carriers, rate, modulation-format and group-id. carriers is the list of carriers bound to the facility, a string of length 1..32. rate is the carried signal basic rate class in Gbit/s. modulation-format is one of not-applicable, DP-QPSK, DP-16QAM, DP-8QAM, BPSK. group-id indicates the interface group instance the FlexO-x interface belongs to and must be unique in the NE, range 1..1048575. Optional on add are label (0..256), admin-state (lock/unlock/maintenance, default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed) and fec-type (not-applicable, cfec, ofec, noFEC, G709, i4, i7, sdfec15, sdfec15nd, staircase7, ufec7; default ofec). set additionally accepts expected-gid, flexo-type, loopback and loopback-mode. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

high-speed-monitoring has just two attributes, both set and show: enabled and port. enabled is the user configurable switch that turns high speed monitoring on or off, values true or false, default false. port is the user configurable port used by the function, a uint16 in the range 1..max with default 57500. Syntax is set high-speed-monitoring [enabled <value>] [port <value>] and show high-speed-monitoring [enabled] [port]. Access mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

interlaken represents the SPN2 Interlaken interface facility; it is a system created facility (managed-by is system only). capacity is a read-only attribute giving the total capacity for the interlaken interface, 500 Gbit/s, which is also its default. The only editable attributes are label (string 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited; default allowed) and loopback (none, facility for a test towards the facility side, terminal for a test towards the terminal side; default none). show also returns supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, AID, oper-state and avail-state. Example: set interlaken-66-1-8 label interlaken_66_1. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode.

On line-ptp, auto-in-service-enabled is the auto-in-service switch for the facility, values true or false, default false, available on add, set and show. valid-signal-time is the configurable time that represents detection of a valid signal and is used by the auto-in-service mechanism; the range is 1..7200 minutes and the default is 480. remaining-valid-signal-time is read-only and shows the actual time left before the facility is automatically enabled by the auto-in-service mechanism, also in the 1..7200 minute range. Set them with add or set line-ptp-<name> auto-in-service-enabled <value> valid-signal-time <value>. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. When auto-in-service is running, avail-state can report auto-in-service.

They are two different commands. network-xconnect is show only: show network-xconnect lists the services of the multiple user cross connections commissioned in this NE; it has no parameters and runs in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. nw-xconnect is the configurable object: add nw-xconnect-<name> endpoint1 <value> endpoint2 <value> [xcon-type <value>] [rate <value>], plus set (rate only), delete and show nw-xconnect-<name> [AID] [oper-state] [avail-state] [endpoint1] [endpoint2] [xcon-type] [rate]. So use nw-xconnect to create, modify or remove an individual user channel cross-connection, and network-xconnect to list the commissioned cross connections on the node.

nw-xconnect supports four xcon-type values and none of them joins a GCC to an OSC: L1-ETH-TO-GCC0, L1-GCC0-TO-GCC0, L1-ETH-TO-OSC and L1-OSC-TO-OSC; the default is L1-GCC0-TO-GCC0. GCC to GCC uses add nw-xconnect-<name> xcon-type L1-GCC0-TO-GCC0 endpoint1 comm-channel-ch1 endpoint2 comm-channel-ch2; OSC to OSC uses xcon-type L1-OSC-TO-OSC with two OSCX-5 comm-channel endpoints, for example endpoint1 comm-channel-2-5-dwdm-line1-OSCX5 endpoint2 comm-channel-2-5-dwdm-line2-OSCX5. endpoint1 and endpoint2 are mandatory instance-identifiers at creation. rate is the maximum user channel bandwidth, 1..20 Mbps, default 13 for L1-ETH-TO-GCC0 and 20 for L1-ETH-TO-OSC and L1-OSC-TO-OSC.

No. The high order ODU is automatically created when an SCH is created; when a CHM6 has an OTU configured on it, use show odu to determine whether the ODU exists. What you create yourself are the low order ODUs, ODU4i (100G) or ODUflexi (400G), which the XCONs are mapped into, and the documented pre-condition is that the super-channel must be added before low order ODUs can be added. The class attribute is system-set: high-order for the top-most ODUCn/ODUk the system creates, low-order (the default) for children, mapped for a mapped client signal. Create a LO-ODU with add odu-<name> odu-type <value> parent-odu <name> [time-slots <value>] [trib-port-number <value>], for example add odu-1-1 odu-type ODU4i parent-odu '1-7-L1-1-ODUCni' time-slots 1..80.

Yes. odu-diagnostics is keyed as odu-diagnostics-<name>/<direction> where direction is ingress or egress, and each direction has its own values. Use add or set odu-diagnostics-<name>/<direction> with tx-tti, expected-tti, tx-sapi, tx-dapi, tx-operator, expected-sapi, expected-dapi and expected-operator. tti-style selects the format: ITU-T-G709 (default), where the TTI splits into SAPI, DAPI and OPER bytes, or proprietary, a single 64 byte string. tx-tti and expected-tti take a hex string with 0x prefix (1..130 characters) or printable ASCII (1..64); SAPI and DAPI are 1..15 ASCII (hex 1..32) and operator 1..32 ASCII (hex 1..66); the expected-* fields default to empty. Example: set odu-diagnostics-Lodu4i/ingress tti-mismatch-alarm-reporting SAPIDAPI-OPER.

Yes, FEC is on by default. On the otu facility fec-mode is the configured Forward Error Correction mode on the OTUk/OTUCn client with values enabled or disabled, and the default is enabled. fec-generation-mode, the FEC generation mode towards the far-end receiver, is also enabled/disabled with default enabled. fec-type selects the FEC and takes not-applicable, cfec, ofec, G709, noFEC, i4, i7, sdfec15, sdfec15nd, staircase7 or ufec7; the default is ofec. All three are available on add, set and show, for example set otu-<name> fec-mode disabled or show otu-<name> fec-mode fec-generation-mode fec-type. Access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Set the tti-mismatch-alarm-reporting attribute on otu-diagnostics to SAPI so the TIM alarm is raised only on a Source Access Point Identifier mismatch: set otu-diagnostics-<name>/<direction> tti-mismatch-alarm-reporting SAPI, for example set otu-diagnostics-1-4-L1-1-OTUCni/ingress tti-mismatch-alarm-reporting SAPI. The attribute indicates whether the TTI-Mismatch (TIM) alarm is reported or masked and, if reported, the criteria used. Values are disabled (default, alarm masked), full-64-bytes, SAPI, DAPI, OPER, SAPI_DAPI, SAPI_OPER, DAPI_OPER and SAPI_DAPI_OPER. Configure the expected value with expected-sapi and keep tti-style at ITU-T-G709 (the default) so the TTI is split into SAPI, DAPI and OPER bytes. Each direction (ingress, egress) has its own values.

The stm facility reports stm-type, the type of SDH signal (STM-N), and the supported values are STM-16 and STM-64; it is a read-only show attribute. The name of the facility is the Synchronous Transport Module N, for example N=16 or 64, per ITU-T G.691. Related trib-ptp service-type values also list STM16 and STM64. Settable STM attributes are label, admin-state (Lock, Unlock, Maintenance; default Unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed), tx-mapping-mode and expected-mapping-mode, tti-style (ITU-T-G709 default, or proprietary), tim-monitor (enabled/disabled, default disabled), tx-tti and expected-tti (tti-64), loopback and loopback-mode (none, facility, terminal; default none), test-signal-type, test-signal-direction and test-signal-monitoring. Example: set stm-1-5-T9.2 tx-mapping-mode BMP.

The trib-ptp attribute tributary-disable-action defines what the network element does towards the client equipment connected over the TOM when a line-side failure is observed, either shutting off the laser or inserting a replacement signal. Values are laser-shut-off (default), none, odu-ais, send-ais-1, send-gais, send-idles, send-lf, send-ms-ais and send-nos (1830 GX G30 only). tributary-disable-holdoff-timer sets the hold off time of the client shutdown or replacement signal in the egress direction, range 0..10000 milliseconds, default 0 meaning holdoff disabled; it applies only when the TDA action is laser-turnoff. Related switches: near-end-tda (enabled/disabled, default disabled), tda-degrade-mode (default disabled) and forward-defect-trigger (true/false, default true). Example: set trib-ptp-1-5-T2 tributary-disable-action laser-shut-off.

Create a Layer 1 digital cross connect with add xcon-<name> source <value> destination <value> [payload-type <value>] [direction <value>] [label <value>] [circuit-id-suffix <value>]; source and destination are instance IDs of the two end-points, for example add xcon-1 source ethernet-1-4-T1 destination odu-1-4-T1-1-ODUni-1. direction only supports two-way, which is also the default. payload-type covers 100GBE, 400GBE, OTU4, 100G, ODU2, ODU2e and empty. set only changes label and circuit-id-suffix; delete xcon-<name> removes it, and only user created XCONs can be user deleted. protection-type is a read-only show attribute representing the protection this XCON has, with values y-cable, snc-n, snc-i and unprotected; the default is unprotected. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

An L2-bridge is identified by bridge-name, a string of length 0..64 used in the entity name L2-bridge-<bridge-name>. Only set and show are available: set L2-bridge-<bridge-name> [chassis-name <value>] [description <value>] and show L2-bridge-<bridge-name> [chassis-name] [description]. There are just two configurable attributes: chassis-name, a leafref giving the chassis associated with this L2 bridge, and description, a string of length 0..255 describing the bridge and its intended purpose. Neither has a default. Access mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Use the clear app command: clear [-f] app [app-name=]<value>. app-name is the third party app name. The -f flag forces the command without confirmation, otherwise the command prompts. Access mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. clear app is the only form documented for the app entity; to control rather than remove a third-party application, use the appctl command with commands restart, netls or exec.

Use appctl [app-name=]<value> [command=]<value> [[target=]<value>] [[parameters=]<value>[,<value>]*]. app-name is the third party app name, a leafref to the third-party-app app-name under system sw-management. command is mandatory and takes restart (restarts the third party application), netls (shows the list of subnet networks used by the containers) or exec (executes a third party application operation given in parameters). target says whether the command is executed for the entire system or for a chassis/card AID; it is a string or the value system, and the default is system. parameters are optional values passed with the command, applicable when command is restart or exec, with max-elements 50. Access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.
